condition: you have to run the model on infrastructure you operate yourself
statement: Meta publishes downloadable weights for Llama 4 Scout under the Llama 4 Community License Agreement, so it can be deployed on hardware the operator controls rather than reached only through a vendor API.
scope: Covers how the weights may be obtained and run. It says nothing about output quality, cost, or the terms of any hosted offering built on these weights.
caveats: Downloadable weights are not an OSI-approved open-source licence; the agreement carries conditions of its own.
This statement rests on availability facts alone: it is derived from the release's access and licence records, not from any benchmark result or usage observation.

condition: your product will pass 700 million monthly active users without a separate agreement with Meta
statement: Section 2 of the Llama 4 Community License Agreement requires a separate licence from Meta above 700 million monthly active users, and the published agreement does not itself grant that licence.
scope: Covers the licence condition as published. It does not describe what terms Meta grants on request, which are not public.
caveats: The threshold is measured by the licence's own definition of monthly active users, not by any figure recorded here.
Licence terms change between model generations; this reading applies to the Llama 4 agreement only.

condition: you plan to depend on the full 10,000,000-token context window the model card documents
statement: The documented context window states what the interface accepts, not how well the model uses it; ModelTree records no measured evidence of retrieval quality across that length for this release.
scope: Covers the stated input limit only. Serving platforms may accept less, and no long-context evaluation is recorded here.
caveats: A stated context window is a documented interface limit, not a measurement of behaviour.
No long-context benchmark result is recorded for this release, so the gap is stated rather than filled by inference.

condition: you need a model you can adopt without vendor approval
statement: Anthropic records Claude Mythos 5 as a preview release available through Project Glasswing approval, so access depends on being accepted rather than on signing up.
scope: Covers the recorded availability stage and the use the documentation states it is offered for. It makes no claim about the model's behaviour.
caveats: Preview availability can change without a new release, so this reading is only as current as its verification date.
The documented intended use is defensive cybersecurity work; other uses are outside what the cited pages describe.

condition: you need a release the vendor's own pages still record as current
statement: Claude Haiku 4.5 is recorded as a current release, and no retirement date is asserted for it here.
scope: Covers the recorded lifecycle stage of this release only.
caveats: The family this release belongs to is recorded as legacy, which is tracked as a conflicting statement rather than resolved.
A lifecycle stage is a vendor label, not a commitment about how long the model remains available.

condition: you are planning a deployment that has to outlast the current model generation
statement: The Claude 4.5 family this release belongs to is recorded as legacy, so the release-level and family-level lifecycle records point in different directions and migration may be needed sooner than the release label suggests.
scope: Covers the recorded lifecycle stage of the family. It does not assert a retirement date, because none is recorded.
caveats: The vendor's own pages disagree: the deprecation table lists the model identifier as active while the models overview groups the 4.5 generation as legacy.
Both readings are kept and neither is treated as correcting the other.

condition: you are starting new work rather than maintaining an existing integration
statement: OpenAI's model documentation labels GPT-5 a previous model and points users to GPT-5.6, and the release is recorded as legacy here.
scope: Covers the recorded lifecycle stage. It does not compare GPT-5's behaviour with any later release, because no evaluation is recorded here.
caveats: No shutdown date is recorded, so existing integrations are not stated to be at risk on any particular date.
A vendor pointing to a newer model is a lifecycle fact, not a measured difference in capability.
